title: Mock NSF panel review
summary: A mock panel summary: strengths and weaknesses under Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts with an overall rating, plus a separate compliance result (15-page limit, Broader Impacts heading, no URLs, Results from Prior NSF Support, DMSP). Checks the Broader Impacts plan and that the DMSP covers the data the plan produces.

values.label: Not compliant: may be returned without review

notAssessed: Biographical sketches, Current and Pending (Other) Support, Facilities
Project Summary (checked for presence only if included)
Human subjects, vertebrate animals and other special information
notes: The five-level rating (Excellent to Poor) is confirmed in secondary sources only; check it against the current NSF reviewer form.
The solicitation governs where it differs from the PAPPG (PAPPG 24-1 with Supplements 1 and 2, NSF 26-200 and 26-202).
Page counts are estimated from words; figures and formatting are not counted.
DMSP tool prompts are taken from NSF Engineering guidance and may vary by directorate; check the live Research.gov form.
The PI decides what to revise and the institution's authorized representative submits; there is no checkpoint.

inputs.label: Program solicitation or program description
inputs.help: Link or cite the solicitation or program description (e.g. NSF 25-xxx). It governs where it differs from the PAPPG, including page limits and extra review criteria.

inputs.label: PAPPG version in force
inputs.help: PAPPG 24-1 with Supplements 1 and 2 was in force when this workflow was checked; note the version the solicitation names.

checks.label: Project Description within 15 pages (incl. Results from Prior NSF Support)
Results from Prior NSF Support within 5 pages

config.instructions: These are PAPPG compliance checks; NSF can return a non-compliant proposal without review. Use the requirements given and the solicitation where linked.

checklist.label: "Broader Impacts" heading on its own line
checklist.question: Does the Project Description contain a separate section with "Broader Impacts" as a heading on its own line?

checklist.label: No URLs in the Project Description
checklist.question: Is the Project Description free of URLs (web addresses)? Name any found.

checklist.label: Prior support reported when required
checklist.question: If the notes or sources show any PI or co-PI has current NSF funding or an award that ended in the past five years, are Results from Prior NSF Support given? Answer not_applicable when there is no such award.

checklist.label: Prior support items and separate headings
checklist.question: Do the Results from Prior NSF Support give award number, amount, period, title, results under separate Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts headings, publications (or none), and research products? Answer not_applicable when the section is absent and not required.

checklist.label: DMSP present
checklist.question: Is a Data Management and Sharing Plan present (drafted here for the Research.gov tool)?

checklist.label: No narrative moved out to dodge the limit
checklist.question: Is there any sign that narrative was moved into references, appendices or other documents to get around the page limit?

checklist.label: Named activities
checklist.question: Are the Broader Impacts activities specific and named, each tied to a societal outcome?

checklist.label: Who carries them out
checklist.question: Does each activity say who carries it out, including partners?

checklist.label: Resources
checklist.question: Are the resources for each activity (people, partners, budget, facilities) stated?

checklist.label: How success is assessed
checklist.question: Does each activity say how its success will be assessed?

checklist.label: Open to all
checklist.question: Is any participation, outreach or recruitment activity limited to a group defined by a protected characteristic? NSF's priorities statement says such activities must be open to all Americans. Answer not_met and name the activity if so.

config.instructions: List each kind of data, sample, software or other research product the plan says the project will produce or collect.

fields.name: product
fields.label: Data or product
fields.description: The data type or product as named

fields.name: objective
fields.label: Objective
fields.description: The objective or activity that produces it

checklist.label: Covered by the DMSP
checklist.question: Does the Data Management and Sharing Plan have an entry covering this data or product, with access, archiving and a timeline?

checklist.label: Research.gov prompts answered
checklist.question: For each data or product category, does the plan answer the tool's prompts: access policies and limitations, data standards and metadata, provenance, public archiving, timeline for public accessibility, data availability and accountability?

checklist.label: Publication data shared at publication
checklist.question: Does the plan share data supporting publications at the time of publication, or describe and justify the exception?

checklist.label: Consistent with the methods
checklist.question: Does anything in the plan contradict the Research Plan (data types, volumes, sensitive data, timing)?

checklist.label: One plan for a collaborative proposal
checklist.question: If this is a collaborative proposal or has subawards, is there one combined plan? Answer not_applicable otherwise.

checklist.label: A no-plan statement is justified
checklist.question: If the plan says no detailed plan is needed, is that clearly justified? Answer not_applicable otherwise.

criteria.label: Intellectual Merit
criteria.guidance: The potential to advance knowledge, judged on the five review elements: potential, creativity and originality, a sound plan with a mechanism to assess success, qualifications, resources.

criteria.label: Broader Impacts
criteria.guidance: The potential to benefit society, judged on the same five elements.

criteria.label: Overall rating
criteria.guidance: Your overall rating, weighing both criteria.

config.instructions: Write strengths and weaknesses under Intellectual Merit and under Broader Impacts, as an NSF panelist would, each tied to a passage. Consider the DMSP under either criterion. Make no prediction about funding.

reviewers.label: Panelist in the field
reviewers.brief: You are a panelist working in this subfield. Judge whether the objectives would genuinely advance knowledge, whether the approach is original, and whether the methods and qualifications fit. Name the specific scientific weaknesses an expert would see.

reviewers.label: Panelist from an adjacent field
reviewers.brief: You are a panelist from a neighbouring discipline. Judge how clearly the case for importance reads to a scientist outside the subfield, and weigh the Broader Impacts plan: who benefits, how, with what resources and how success is measured.

reviewers.label: Skeptical panelist
reviewers.brief: Test the plan: is it well reasoned and organized, is there a real mechanism to assess success, are the resources and timeline adequate, and are there risks with no alternative? Rate from the weaknesses you find.

config.guidance: Write the panel summary: strengths and weaknesses under Intellectual Merit, then under Broader Impacts, then the overall rating the agreement supports. Report disagreements with each rationale; do not average. Choose not_compliant only when a compliance or page-limit finding is blocking; then list the compliance problems first and still give the panel's rating in the rationale.

guards.reason: a blocking compliance finding (page limit, Broader Impacts heading or missing DMSP) can lead NSF to return the proposal without review.
